intro: What people believe and decide depends on the information they encounter, and AI and platforms increasingly shape it. I am a computational social scientist working to build healthier information environments for democratic societies. Using AI and information systems, I design and test ways to expand access to trustworthy information while limiting exposure to untrustworthy sources, to represent a broader range of information and perspectives, and to support an informed citizenry.
My work is organized around three themes:

callout.label: Dissertation
callout.text: Leveraging AI-Mediated Information Environments for Democracy

themes.title: Access: Shaping What Information Is Easy to Reach
themes.summary: Making trustworthy information easier to reach and untrustworthy sources harder to reach.

subthemes.title: Limiting Exposure to Untrustworthy Sources
subthemes.description: A small share of users account for most engagement with untrustworthy sources. I test two ways to durably improve their information consumption: muting those sources for them, or giving them media literacy tips.

items.title: Mercury: data-collection and intervention pipeline for the muting field experiment

subthemes.title: Facilitating Access to Trusted Information
subthemes.description: Voters trust local election officials most, but their reach is limited. I test whether a chatbot that delivers official information improves voter knowledge, trust, and beliefs about elections.

items.title: Evaluating Accuracy and Safety of Election Chatbot
items.authors: Megan Lu, Vashawn Robinson, Ryan Yu, Lina Romero-Fabian, Johnny Zhu, Do Won Kim, Giovanni Luca Ciampaglia, Cody Buntain

themes.title: Representation: Broadening the Information and Perspectives People Encounter
themes.summary: Broadening the information and perspectives available to people.

subthemes.title: Creating Unexpected Partisan Encounters
subthemes.description: Partisans expect co-partisans to be like them and opponents to be different, a distorted view that fuels polarization. I test whether AI conversations that defy these expectations reduce polarization without persuading anyone on the issues.

subthemes.title: Designing Feeds Beyond Engagement
subthemes.description: What drives engagement often diverges from what users say they value. I design and test feeds that better reflect the stated preferences of users and encourage civil engagement across divides.

items.title: Understanding the Gap Between Stated and Revealed Preferences in Social Media News Feeds

subthemes.title: Scholarly Information Environments
subthemes.description: Science is an information environment too, with the same questions: what gets seen, by whom, and through which systems. I study whose knowledge becomes visible across languages, and which infrastructures shape how research is found and shared.

themes.title: Informed Citizenry: Supporting Political Learning and Participation
themes.summary: Helping citizens learn about politics and make informed political decisions.

subthemes.title: Political Learning with AI
subthemes.description: More people now learn about politics through AI. I compare direct exposure to political information, AI-generated summaries, and conversational AI assistance to test whether AI mediation improves how people understand a complex policy issue.

items.title: Learning Politics with AI: Political Knowledge, Institutional Trust, and Attitudes Toward Interbranch Conflict
